findings.claim: Criterion 5 is not met. When no SurrogateType is given, the collector always builds contractless members and never reads attributes on T. A referenced T that carries [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[IgnoreDataMember] gets a string-keyed map of every public read-write member. Ignored members (for example a secret) are serialized, declared int keys are replaced by member-name string keys, and the wire format differs from what the type's own attributes define.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129GeneratedFormatterAttributesTests (MessagePackObjectIgnoreMemberOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured, DataContractOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured). Each asserts that the ignored or non-DataMember property 'HiddenSecret' does not appear in the generated formatter; on head it does.

findings.claim: Contractless mode keeps only public read-write members. Getter-only public properties and readonly public fields are dropped completely, so they are not even serialized, which loses data silently. The requirement asks for 'contractless behaviour over public members', and MessagePack's existing contractless mode serializes such members.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a referenced type with `public int Id { get; }` plus a matching constructor, or with only `public int Id { get; }`. Assert that the generated Serialize writes 'Id'; on head it is absent.

findings.claim: A referenced class whose only accessible constructor takes parameters is rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor, and constructorParameters is always empty. Contractless behaviour in MessagePack matches constructor parameters to members, so immutable library types (common in a 'minimal, zero-dependency' Project A) cannot get a generated formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Project A: `public class P { public P(int id) { Id = id; } public int Id { get; set; } }`. Project B: a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.P>. Assert that the output compilation has no errors and that a formatter is generated; on head a diagnostic is reported and no implementation is emitted, so CS0535 occurs.

questions.text: Must contractless mode for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] match MessagePack's existing contractless semantics: serialize getter-only public members and deserialize through parameterized constructors?
options: Yes, match the existing contractless resolver behaviour
No, read-write members plus a parameterless constructor are enough for this feature
questions.why_it_matters: If yes, the getter-only and constructor findings are real requirement gaps (medium). If no, they become documented limitations and are dropped.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Contractless by default over public read-write members. Keys and membership are customised only through a new `SurrogateType` property on [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], whose [Key]/[IgnoreMember] members are matched to T by name and type (GeneratedFormatterCollector.CreateSurrogateMembers, plus MsgPack022).

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: No surrogate. Keys and membership come from attributes on T itself, per issue alternative 1 and the maintainer note. When surrogate is null, GeneratedFormatterCollector first checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[IgnoreDataMember] and builds members from them (as the existing TypeCollector does for source types). It falls back to CreateContractlessMembers only when T has neither attribute. SurrogateType and MsgPack022 are dropped.
